memos.headline: S06 and S09 Near Highs With Relative Strength; S01 and S02 Structurally Weak
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe heading into year-end. S06 at 327.91 is just -0.4% off its 52-week high with RSI 63.6 and the strongest 4-week relative strength vs SPY at +5.0%—this is a textbook trend-continuation setup and I have high conviction here. S09 at 119.11 is similarly positioned only -0.6% from its high, with positive relative strength across both 4w (+2.2%) and 12w (+3.1%) windows and moderate RSI of 56.3, making it a clean long. On the other side, S01 is in a persistent downtrend: -10.1% over 26 weeks, trading 7.5% below its 200-day mean, with 12w relative strength vs SPY at -8.8%—I would avoid until it reclaims its 200-day average. S02's -44.6% drawdown from its 52-week high and position 5.7% below its 200-day mean signal severe structural damage despite a recent bounce; I need to see it sustain above the 200-day mean before reconsidering.

Massive 26w return of +59.2% and 12w relative strength of +18.0% vs SPY, but +35.2% above 200d mean raises mean-reversion risk; would cut on a close below 550.

Orderly uptrend with +5.4% over 12w and modest RSI of 55.3, but -8.5% drawdown and flat 4w relative strength leave me without strong conviction either way.
Trading 2.1% below 50d mean with 12w relative strength of -9.4% vs SPY and -10% drawdown from high; would reconsider above 500.
Persistent downtrend: -10.1% over 26w, 7.5% below 200d mean, 12w relative strength -8.8% vs SPY; need a sustained reclaim of the 200d average (~156) to change my view.
Catastrophic -44.6% drawdown from 52w high and trading 5.7% below 200d mean signals broken structure; avoid until price sustains above the 200d mean.
Strong 1w bounce of +9.4% and 4w relative strength of +4.1%, but still -8% from high and 12w relative strength is -1.5%; watching for follow-through above 195 to turn long.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Superior Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Face Margin Compression
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin compounders and names where earnings quality is deteriorating. S10 stands out with 56% net margins, +62.5% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt at $8.47B — this is the strongest fundamental profile in the group by a wide margin. S05 also impresses with 34.2% net margins, +33% YoY net income growth, and a clean balance sheet ($14.79B debt on $102B revenue). On the other end, S02 posted a 2.1% net margin with net income collapsing -61.2% YoY despite +12.2% revenue growth, signaling severe cost or impairment issues against $80.14B in debt. S09 is the only name with negative revenue growth (-5.2% YoY) and shrinking earnings (-12.3%), and its 8.8% margin leaves little cushion. I would need to see margin stabilization in S02 and a return to top-line growth in S09 before reconsidering either.

views.note: 56% net margin, +62.5% revenue growth, near-zero leverage — the best earnings power and growth profile in the universe.
34.2% net margin with +33% YoY net income growth and low debt ($14.79B) supports durable earnings compounding.
35.7% net margin and +18.4% revenue growth are strong, though +12.5% net income growth lags revenue, suggesting some margin pressure to watch.
Solid +13.4% revenue growth and +38.2% net income growth, but 11.8% net margin and $55.1B debt keep me from high conviction.
+86.4% YoY net income rebound is impressive but 26.8% margin sits on $90.68B of debt and only +7.9% revenue growth — need to see sustained top-line acceleration.
21.2% margin and +20% net income growth are respectable, but only +3% revenue growth and $24.3B debt on $22.4B revenue limit upside.
31% net margin is healthy but $427.2B total debt dwarfs revenue; earnings growth of +11.6% is modest for that leverage profile.
13% margin and -6.7% net income decline on +9.5% revenue growth suggests cost headwinds; $31.7B debt on $17.6B revenue is elevated.
Revenue declining -5.2% YoY with net income down -12.3% and only 8.8% margin — no evidence of a turnaround yet.
Net income collapsed -61.2% YoY to a razor-thin 2.1% margin despite +12.2% revenue growth; $80.1B debt makes this a clear avoid until margins recover.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Labor Softening and Sticky CPI Argue for a Late-Cycle Posture
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has fallen 75 bp over the past year to 3.75%, with 50 bp of that in the last three months alone, and the 10y yield has followed, dropping 44 bp year-over-year to 4.14%. However, the easing is running into two crosscurrents—CPI is still running at +2.7% y/y, above target, while the unemployment rate has crept up 30 bp y/y to 4.50%, signaling a softening labor market. The 10y-2y spread has steepened 38 bp over the past year to +0.68 pp, which is constructive for banks but also consistent with the market pricing a growth slowdown. I am positioning for a late-cycle environment: favoring duration-sensitive growth and banks that benefit from a steeper curve, staying neutral on staples, and avoiding pure cyclicals that need re-acceleration. A January CPI print above +0.4% m/m or an unemployment rate above 4.7% would force me to reassess toward a more defensive stance.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields (-44 bp y/y) and continued Fed easing.
Banks gain from a steepening curve (+38 bp y/y in 10y-2y spread) and still-positive nominal rate levels.
Staples offer defensive ballast but limited upside given CPI at 2.7% y/y compressing real margins.
Cyclicals face headwinds from rising unemployment (+0.30 y/y) signaling demand softening.
Energy lacks a clear macro catalyst; easing supports demand but labor softening caps upside.
Rate-sensitive sectors benefit as the Fed has cut 75 bp over the past year with more easing likely.

memos.headline: Leadership Churn Dominates 8-K Flow; S10 Earnings Reaction the Only Concrete Negative Signal
memos.body: I reviewed all available 8-K filings across the universe through 2025-12-26. The most notable data point is S10's -3.2% price reaction following its Nov 19 earnings release, which stands out as the only quantifiable negative sentiment event. S09 had a muted -0.3% reaction to its Oct 31 earnings, suggesting the market had already priced in expectations. Multiple names—S08, S06, S04, S09, S01, S02—filed director/officer departure or appointment 8-Ks in November-December, which I read as routine governance activity rather than narrative shifts. Without GDELT tone data or media coverage volume, I have low conviction across the board and am relying solely on 8-K event type and the two price reactions available.

views.note: The -3.2% post-earnings drop on Nov 19-20 signals negative sentiment around operating results that may not yet be fully washed out.
Muted -0.3% earnings reaction and heavy 8-K cadence (5 filings in ~6 weeks) suggest stable but noisy narrative with no clear directional shift.
Three 8-Ks in two weeks (Reg FD, bylaws amendment, officer change) are governance-heavy but lack tone data to distinguish positive from negative.
Back-to-back Other Events filings in early Nov plus a Dec officer change are routine; no price reaction data to gauge sentiment direction.
Dec 8 director change and shareholder vote filing is standard governance; insufficient tone evidence to take a directional view.
Single officer departure/appointment 8-K on Dec 5 provides no sentiment signal without accompanying media tone data.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Plunges 44% in One Month While Oil Slides Below $59—Geopolitical Tailwinds Favor Risk but Energy Stays Pressured
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped sharply to 181.39, down 44% month-over-month, while VIX has collapsed to 13.47 (down 34% in a month), signaling a meaningful de-escalation in policy-driven risk premia heading into year-end. WTI crude at $58.72, off over 10% in three months, suggests either weakening demand expectations or an easing of supply-side geopolitical constraints—neither reading supports a bullish energy thesis near-term. HY spreads at 2.84% have tightened 31bp over the past month, consistent with a benign credit backdrop and no imminent sanctions or trade-war shock being priced. I have moderate conviction that this calm is structural rather than seasonal, but I would reassess quickly if new export controls on semiconductors or a fresh round of China tariffs were announced. The 8-K filings across S01, S02, S03, S05, and S09 are generic Other Events or Reg FD disclosures with no geopolitical red flags surfacing.

views.note: Two 8-Ks in early November with no geopolitical content; low policy uncertainty backdrop is mildly supportive but no specific catalyst.
Three 8-Ks in Oct-Nov (Reg FD and Other Events) show active disclosure but no geopolitical risk signal; benign macro backdrop keeps me neutral.
Falling policy uncertainty and tight HY spreads create a favorable environment; no adverse geopolitical exposure flagged in its 8-K.
Benign geopolitical backdrop with VIX at 13.47 and policy uncertainty down sharply supports risk-on positioning; 8-K was routine.
WTI crude down 10% over three months signals weak energy demand or easing supply constraints—headwind for energy-exposed names absent a geopolitical supply shock.
Reg FD disclosure in November with no geopolitical detail; low conviction either way given limited information.

plan.summary: Positioning for a late-cycle environment with falling policy uncertainty and continued Fed easing by overweighting high-quality compounders near technical highs (S06, S05, S10) and adding rate-sensitive beneficiaries (S03, S04), while keeping meaningful cash given sticky CPI and softening labor. Avoiding structurally damaged names (S01, S02) and energy (S09) where fundamentals are deteriorating.

Technical analyst has high conviction (0.85). Fundamentals are decent (31% margin) though not top-tier, and geopolitics analyst flags energy headwinds but S06 appears more staples/defensive. Net positive across technical and macro.
